על פרס המליצו 60 חברי כנסת להרכבת הממשלה (המערך, יחד, רצ, שינוי, חד"ש, הרשימה המתקדמת ואומץ) בעוד שעל שמיר המליצו 54 (הליכוד, התחייה, ש"ס, אגודת ישראל ומורשה), כשהמפד"ל ואבוחצירא תומכים בממשלת אחדות וכהנא לא הוזמן לבית הנשיא.
60 Knesset members asked Herzog to choose Peres

notes: Per-list split (Alignment 44, Hadash 4, Ratz 3, Yahad 3, Shinui 3, Progressive List 2, Ometz 1 = 60; Likud 41, Tehiya–Tzomet 5, Shas 4, Agudat Yisrael 2, Morasha 2 = 54) matches JTA's contemporary totals; El País counted 59 for Labor (it groups Yahad and Ometz as 'three'), recorded as a source conflict. Recommendations were made on Friday 3 August 1984; Herzog gave Peres the mandate on 5 August. The rotation agreement (Shamir to take over after 25 months) came later and is not a recommendation.

Upgrade: JTA 6 August 1984 names every faction on each side, including Ometz/Hurwitz and the unity-government positions; the per-list classification no longer depends solely on Hebrew Wikipedia. Kach was not invited, not an explicit refusal to recommend.

A later book, Abraham Diskin’s chapter in Israel at the Polls 2009 (Routledge, 2011), p. 61, says 60 MKs backed Peres and 60 backed Shamir. The reports of the time (JTA, 6 and 7 August 1984) give 60 and 54, and this record keeps their figures.

The Knesset record of the vote gives only the totals, so this MK’s own vote is unknown.

cites.quote: The dissenters on the left were Mapam, the Civil Rights Movement (CRM), the Hadash (Communist) Party and the Progressive List for Peace.
A dovish member of the Labor Party, Yossi Sarid, left that party and joined an opposition party, CRM.
on the left (Ratz, Mapam and Yossi Sarid, Hadash and the Progressive List for Peace)
cites.note: Among those outside the coalition.
cites.noteHe: בין אלה שמחוץ לקואליציה.

individuals.note: Elected on the Alignment list but not one of its 37 MKs in the coalition: he left Labor for the Citizens’ Rights Movement, in opposition, as a report of the time and two independent studies say.
